Project: medidor
Purpose: Internet speed measurement toolkit (CLI + desktop GUI + web UI) with CSV/PostgreSQL storage and basic forecasting.

Primary language: Python (3.11+)
Platforms: Windows-first workflows (batch launchers), cross-platform Python scripts.

Key entry points:
- main.py -> Collect speed samples (download/upload/ping)
- gui.py -> Desktop app (customtkinter)
- web_ui.py -> Web app (Streamlit)
- analyze.py -> CSV cleaning/analysis
- train_forecast.py -> Model training
- predict_next.py -> Next-value prediction
- postgres/import_csv.py -> CSV to PostgreSQL
- postgres/export_to_csv.py -> PostgreSQL to CSV

Run commands:
- start_gui.bat
- start_web.bat
- python main.py --samples 5 --interval-seconds 60 --timeout 20 --storage csv
- python analyze.py --input internet_speed_data.csv --rolling-window 5 --output-clean internet_speed_data_clean.csv
- python train_forecast.py --input internet_speed_data.csv --target download_mbps --horizon 1 --lags 5 --test-size 0.2
- python predict_next.py --input internet_speed_data.csv --model models/medidor_forecast.joblib

Data and artifacts:
- Raw CSV: internet_speed_data.csv
- Clean CSV: internet_speed_data_clean.csv
- Models: models/
- Runtime log: app.log

Operational constraints for AI agents:
- Keep changes small and focused.
- Preserve existing CLI argument compatibility unless explicitly requested.
- If argparse interfaces change, update README.md.
- Avoid adding dependencies unless necessary.
- Do not commit generated artifacts (logs, trained models, output CSV) unless requested.
- Validate touched scripts at least with syntax check:
  python -m py_compile main.py gui.py web_ui.py analyze.py train_forecast.py predict_next.py

Preferred docs for orientation:
- README.md
- AGENTS.md

Notes:
- PostgreSQL usage is optional.
- If UI seems to fail silently, inspect app.log first.
